From the identity $1+{cot}^{2}⁡\theta ={csc}^{2}⁡\theta $ with $\theta =x-\frac{\pi }{6},$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}1+{cot}^{2}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{6}) & ={csc}^{2}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{6}) \\ {cot}^{2}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{6}) & ={csc}^{2}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{6})-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our integral gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\pi /3}^{\pi /2}(1-{cot}^{2}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{6}))\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{\pi /3}^{\pi /2}(1-{csc}^{2}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{6})+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /3}^{\pi /2}(2-{csc}^{2}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{6}))\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /3}^{\pi /2}2\,\text{d}x-{\int }_{\pi /3}^{\pi /2}{csc}^{2}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{6})\,\text{d}x \\  & =2x\,{|}_{\pi /3}^{\pi /2}+\operatorname{cot}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{6})\,{|}_{\pi /3}^{\pi /2} \\  & =2(\frac{\pi }{2}-\frac{\pi }{3})+\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}-\frac{\pi }{6})-\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}-\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =2(\frac{\pi }{6})+\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})-\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{3}+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}-\sqrt{3} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{3}-\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
